authoring.repair_policy: regenerate derived files from skill_contract.json and rerun the full gate

capabilities.trigger: Use when writing or reviewing a scientific report for a biomedical or bioinformatics analysis.

entries.claim: Provides report writing standards for biomedical analyses covering structure, discipline, data integrity, evidence tiers, figures, citations, and bioinformatics norms
Defines evidence tier language constraints bounding the strongest sentence a report may write

clarification_questions.prompt: What analysis results do you need to report?
Who is the audience for this report?
What evidence tier does your analysis support?

choices.label: Single cohort, no independent replication (most common)
I am not sure, help me determine

infographic.not_applicable_reason: Guidance skill teaches writing standards; does not generate qualitative infographics

execution.not_applicable_reason: Guidance skill has no scripts to execute; provides prose standards in SKILL.md

external_dependencies.not_applicable_reason: No external services or APIs are called; this is a guidance skill with no computation

facts.not_applicable_reason: Guidance skill: teaches writing standards, does not generate evidence-bearing claims

figures.not_applicable_reason: Guidance skill teaches figure standards but does not generate or declare its own result figures

inference_readiness.not_applicable_reason: Guidance skill: does not perform statistical inference or population-level comparison

resource_identity.not_applicable_reason: Guidance skill does not emit citations, accessions, or external identifiers; it teaches citation standards

inputs: A completed scientific analysis (typically biomedical/bioinformatics) with results requiring documentation
Analysis type: differential expression, survival, variant calling, pathway enrichment, or other
Audience: bench scientist, PI, regulatory, or publication-ready
Evidence tier: validated, hypothesis-generating, or exploratory

workflow.title: Assess report need and determine evidence tier
workflow.instruction: Determine whether a report is warranted based on analysis complexity and user request. Compute the evidence tier from the run: validated requires independent replication, single-cohort is hypothesis-generating, untested is exploratory.

workflow.title: Structure the report content
workflow.instruction: Apply the five mandatory sections (Task Context, Methods and Sources, Results, Conclusions and Interpretation, Limitations) with run-specific content. Derive numbers from artifacts, not hand-typed.

workflow.title: Apply writing discipline and bioinformatics norms
workflow.instruction: Follow derive-not-restate, no-filler, caption, caveat, and bioinformatics-specific rules. Ensure gene IDs, genome build, statistical reporting, normalization, and batch effects are documented.

workflow.title: Generate the PDF report
workflow.instruction: Use phylo-pdf-report-generation or compatible provider to render the structured content into a branded PDF.

caveats.statement: Evidence tier must be computed from the run, not chosen: a single-cohort result labeled validated is always wrong
caveats.evidence_ref: Evidence tier section in the report

caveats.statement: Numbers in prose must derive from artifacts: prose count disagreeing with table count is a defect
Limitations must be run-specific: generic boilerplate that could apply to any experiment is not a limitation

existing_materials: SKILL.md: authored fresh — guidance content covering nine writing standard domains
No scripts: this is a guidance skill with prose standards, not executable code

source_assertions_not_applicable_reason: No external facts are used in computation; this is a guidance skill

starting_task.decision_context: A scientist has completed an analysis and needs to write a report that is rigorous enough to share externally, submit for review, or include in a publication. They need to know the required sections, writing style, evidence tier constraints, and domain-specific conventions.
starting_task.objective: Provide comprehensive guidance on report structure, writing discipline, data integrity, evidence tier language, figure and table standards, citation rules, and bioinformatics-specific reporting norms so the user can produce a rigorous, honest, reproducible report.
starting_task.subject_input: A completed biomedical or bioinformatics analysis (e.g., RNA-seq DE analysis with 412 tested genes, 3 significant at padj < 0.05, one volcano plot, one top-10 results table) that needs to be documented in a structured scientific report.
starting_task.user_prompt: What standards should I follow when writing a scientific report for my biomedical analysis?

auto.evidence: SKILL.md covers all nine content domains with concrete rules and examples; evidence tier language constraints are explicitly defined

guided.reason: No separate child run with user clarification selection has been performed yet
